correctness.rationale: For any double star T_{a,b} with both leaf blocks nonempty, the no-both-hubs subcomplex A is contractible: the entire leaf simplex plus each one-hub cone attaches along a contractible leaf-block join, also covering r=1. Faces containing both hubs are exactly {u,v} union a leaf set S of size <=r-2. In the relative oriented chain complex C_*(X,A), deletion of either hub vanishes; the leaf differential is the augmented boundary on the (r-3)-skeleton of the (m-1)-simplex, shifted by the oriented hub pair and twisted by the sign of any hub exchange. The integral augmented differential is contraction by epsilon on exterior powers of Z^L; splitting Z^L=ker epsilon ⊕ Z e_l0 shows the only relative homology is wedge^(r-2) ker epsilon in degree r-1, with no torsion. The long exact sequence is equivariant because A is invariant and contractible. For r>=m+2 X is the full simplex, and for r=1 X=A is contractible; r=2 gives the correct trivial exterior power with hub sign. The rational character is eta(g)[z^(r-2)] det(I+z P_g)/(1+z), with cycle factors. Independent checks for a=b=3,r=4 gave rank 10, hub-block-swap trace 2, matching the 6+4 eigenspace split. The checked finite example does not replace the proof for all a,b,r.
residual_risks: A non-equivariant wedge decomposition is insufficient to identify this integral group module; the relative oriented-chain proof supplies the extra structure.
The theorem concerns ordinary integral homology as an Aut-lattice, not fixed spaces or an equivariant homotopy equivalence.

value.rationale: The automorphism action is a natural invariant of the double-star family, which has substantial S_a×S_b and sometimes block-exchange symmetry. Identifying the full integral lattice, rather than only rational traces or known ordinary homotopy, distinguishes hub-exchange behavior and provides a reusable character formula simultaneously for all thresholds and leaf sizes. The precise twist matters for any later equivariant or quotient analysis.
residual_risks: The module is for only a two-hub tree; no equivariant wedge decomposition or all-tree module theorem is claimed.
